space-bunny-free.reason: X is tight, well-threaded and genuinely builder-facing, but it repeatedly promotes paraphrase into quotation marks (Mostaque on bad infrastructure, Blundin on data centers, the invented 'utility AI versus the frontier AI' line, McBride on zoning), misattributes the fifteen-percent stock drop to Diamandis, and adds unsourced specifics — a named CNBC reporter, 'seventy-some points' in a prompting guide, Craig Heifetz's Maye verdict, an 'undefeated' Raiders team that contradicts the 0-3 framing, 'this month' for an August arXiv paper — while its build pitch ends by pointing at Kyle's own build-pitches folder, and it spots.Callbacks to yesterday's show land as unnarrated recaps rather than woven-in continuity; Y is exemplary on provenance, flagging its own limits before the show starts ('no speaker labels, so I'm attributing lines only where Peter called on a person by name', 'I only have the title and the point count', 'I only read the abstract'), attributing unconfirmed numbers to the man who said them, and never quoting a document it didn't have — and it converts the same material into more actionable substance (Weil's insurance-disclosure trick, Drake Thomas's boring-vs-cracked evaluators, the deleted-system-prompt pruning pass, the 17%-fall-detection failure, the Humira patent thicket) with a build pitch pitched cleanly in general terms, giving up only some momentum to a much longer middle and a laundry-list lightning round that dilutes the episode's pacing.

opus.reason: X attributes its claims carefully and flags each source limit, and it goes deep on Zvi, Moonshots, the Claude Code harness, Odd Lots and Attia with a well-sourced, general build pitch; it is long and pads the sports and entertainment sections with headline copy, and 'Jev' reads like a transcription slip. Y is tighter and turns the news into useful practices for builders, but it overstates or adds details the sources may not support (the fall becomes 'insurance stocks', the Raiders become 'undefeated', a Craig Heifetz attribution, Norris 'regretted' his comments, a German election aside), and its build pitch names Kyle's own build-pitches folder, which breaks the rule against describing the listener's private setup.
